chunks: And what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated, he said: Some of our companions informed me that he asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) during the ten days of Shawwal.

He said: I intend to perform an independent Umrah this month. He said to him: You are held hostage by the Hajj. The man said to him: Indeed, Medina is my home and Mecca is my home, and I have family between them and wealth between them. He said to him: You are held hostage by the Hajj. The man said to him: Indeed, I have orchards around Mecca and I need to go out to them. He said: You go out permissible and return permissible to the Hajj.

The correct view regarding these two narrations is one of two things: either we interpret them as indicating a type of recommendation, or we interpret them as referring to one whose Umrah is Tamattu', for it is not permissible for him to go out because he is held hostage by the Hajj, according to what the two narrations contain. And in the two narrations it is not specified whether the Umrah was independent or the one performed for Tamattu' until Hajj; rather, it is general, and we interpret them with this distinction so that the narrations do not contradict each other, which indicates this meaning.

key_terms.شَوَّال: Shawwal (the tenth month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.مُتْعَة: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined with a break)
key_terms.مُرْتَهَنٌ بِالْحَجِّ: Held hostage by the Hajj (obligated to remain in the state of Ihram for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim perform an independent Umrah during the days of Hajj if they are already committed to the Hajj ritual?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction in these narrations by distinguishing between an independent Umrah (which is recommended) and the Umrah of Tamattu' (which binds the pilgrim to the Hajj state). This juristic nuance clarifies that while a Mutamatti' is 'held hostage' by their Hajj obligation and cannot leave for trivial matters, they may depart for essential needs like family or property, ensuring the coherence of the legal rulings on pilgrimage obligations.
